reference.title: Band Seated Lateral Raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen; the band is hardest at the top, where it is stretched most
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower lowering, a stronger band, or the feet wider on the band

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench, feet flat and wide with the band under the balls of the feet; one end in each hand beside the bench, palms in, elbows soft.
Breathe out and raise the arms out to the sides, a little in front of the body, thumbs forward.
Stop at about shoulder height, elbows level with the hands; shoulders down while the band is tightest.
Lower slowly in about 2 s against the band.
Brief pause beside the bench with a little tension left in the band, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the trunk to start the lift
mistakes.fix: Sit tall and still; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging toward the ears as the band gets tight
mistakes.fix: Reach the hands long and out.

mistakes.mistake: Feet sliding so the band slips off
mistakes.fix: Keep the feet flat and pressed down on the band.

kinematics.norm: From beside the bench to about 90 degrees (the range used by Coratella 2020; impingement study 2014)
About 30 degrees in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane; clinical opinion)
Upright on the end of a flat bench, knees about 90 degrees, feet flat (clinical opinion)
Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest near the top; at matched effort, elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar deltoid activity in a lateral raise (Andersen 2010)
2 s up, 0.5 s pause, 2 s down in Coratella 2020

sources.title: GymVisual #16966, Band Seated Lateral Raise, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Characteristics of shoulder impingement in the recreational weight-training population (J Strength Cond Res 2014;28(4):1081-1089, PubMed 24077379)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Check the band for nicks or tears and keep the feet pressed on it so it cannot slip out and snap up.
Band tension is user-chosen: pick one you can control through the whole range.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The cited EMG studies used standing raises; the seated version is assumed to load the deltoids similarly with less body swing (clinical opinion).
modify: Pinching at the top: stop at about 70-80 degrees.
Low-back fatigue: sit against an upright back pad.
progressions: Stronger band or feet wider apart.
Slower lowering or a 2 s hold at the top.

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Main mover. The lateral raise gave the highest medial deltoid activity of the exercises tested (Campos 2020); "thumbs forward" gave the highest medial deltoid activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2020). Those studies tested standing raises. At matched effort elastic tubing gave deltoid activity similar to dumbbells (Andersen 2010); with a band the load peaks near the top.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Main mover. The lateral raise gave the highest medial deltoid activity of the exercises tested (Campos 2020); "thumbs forward" gave the highest medial deltoid activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2020). Those studies tested standing raises. At matched effort elastic tubing gave deltoid activity similar to dumbbells (Andersen 2010); with a band the load peaks near the top.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps lift the arms, more so if they drift forward (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps lift the arms, more so if they drift forward (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades near the top.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades near the top.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk tall without back support; sitting removes leg drive and swinging (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the spine tall on the unsupported seat.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the spine tall on the unsupported seat.
